 THESE APPEALS, COMING ON FOR ADMISSION, THIS DAY, THE COURT DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 JUDGMENT These two appeals are filed by the appellants- claimants challenging the judgment and award passed by the Senior Civil Judge and MACT at Kundapura in MVC Nos.444/2013 and 445/2013, dated 06.04.2015.
2.

The brief factual matrix leading to the case are that on 05.03.2013 at about 9.30 p.m., the deceased Chandra Shekar was riding his motor cycle bearing registration No.20-EA-3165 along with pillion rider Ravindra, who was claimant in MVC No.445/2013 from Kundapura towards Byndoor side.

When they reached near Vaibhava Bar and Restaurant, Talluru Village, at that time, driver of the bus bearing registration No.KA-25/C-9558, NC: 2023:KHC:41430 drove it in a rash and negligent manner and in a very high speed and dashed to the motor cycle, resulting in the accident.
As the result of this impact, Chandra Shekar in MVC No.444/2013 was succumbed at the spot and claimant Ravindra in MVC No.445/2013 suffered grievous injuries.
3. The Legal heirs of the deceased- Chandra Shekar and claimant- Ravindra filed claim petitions under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 claiming compensation of Rs.15,00,000/- each.
4. The claim petitions were contested by respondent No.3- Insurance Company and the policy came to be admitted.
But, the actionable negligence on the part of the driver of the offending vehicle came to be disputed, asserting that the accident is because of the actionable negligence on the part of the deceased.
Hence, they have sought for dismissal of the claim petition.
5. The Tribunal after appreciating the oral and documentary evidence, allowed both the petitions in part.

The claimants in MVC No.444/2013 were awarded total compensation of Rs.5,76,500/-, while claimant in MVC No.445/2013 was awarded total compensation of Rs.2,84,680/- by fastening liability on respondent No.3 - Insurance Company.
6. Being aggrieved by these judgments and awards passed by the Tribunal, the claimants are before this Court seeking enhancement by way of these appeals.
7. MFA No.4716/2015 is filed by the Legal Heirs of the deceased, while MFA No.4717/2015 is filed by the injured claimant Ravindra.
Since both these claim petitions are arising out of common judgment arising out of the same accident, they are heard together.
8. Heard the arguments advanced by the learned counsel for the appellant and the learned counsel for respondent No.3 - Insurance Company and perused the records.

sentences.text:
The learned counsel for the appellant would contend that the compensation awarded by the Tribunal pertaining to the deceased Chandra Shekar is meager and no future prospects were added,
which has resulted in miscarriage of Justice.
He would also contend that in case of injury, the income was taken on lower side and the loss of future prospects was on lower side and hence, he would seek for enhancement.
10. Per contra, the learned counsel for respondent No.3 - Insurance Company would support the judgment and award passed by the Tribunal.
11. Having heard the arguments and perusing the records, it is evident that MVC No.444/2013 is filed pertaining to the death of one Chandra Shekar.
The claimant No.1 is the mother, claimants No.2, 3 and 4 claims to be the sisters and claimant No.5 claims to be the brother.
It is relevant to the note here that all the three sisters are married and claimant No.5 - Ganesh is the major brother.
Hence, they cannot be termed as NC: 2023:KHC:41430 dependents.
As such, claimant No.1 alone is to be treated as a dependent.
12. The records disclose that the deceased was drawing a salary Rs.6,500/- p.m., when the accident was occurred.
There is no serious dispute about this aspect and infact, it is on lower side.
But, from records it is evident that, the deceased was drawing a salary of Rs.6,500/- p.m.
Since the deceased was aged about 31 years at the time of the accident.
40% is required to be added towards future prospects.
Considering his age as 31, multiplier is 16 needs to be applied.
If the notional income of the deceased is taken as Rs.6,500/- and if, 40% is added towards future prospect, his monthly income would be Rs.9,100/-.
Since he is a bachelor, half of the same is required to be deducted towards his personal expenses and hence, he would have contributed Rs.4,550/- towards maintenance of the family.

Hence, the loss of dependency would work out as Rs.4,550/- x 12 x 16=
Rs.8,73,600/-.
Since claimant No.1 is the mother, she is entitled for Rs.40,000/- under the head of Loss of Consortium.
Under NC: 2023:KHC:41430 the conventional head of funeral expenses and loss of estate, claimant No.1 is also entitled for Rs.30,000/-.

Hence, claimant No.1 in MVC No.444/2013 (MFA No.4716/2015) is entitled for total compensation under various heads as under:
1. Loss of dependency Rs.8,73,600/-
2. Loss of consortium Rs.40,000/-
3. Transportation and funeral Rs.30,000/-
expenses Total Rs.9,43,600/-

Hence, the claimant would be entitled for compensation Rs.9,43,600/- as against Rs.5,76,500/-
awarded by the Tribunal.

sentences.text: As regards, in MFA No.4717/2015 arising out of MVC No.445/2013, the claimant is the injured.
The records disclose that, he suffered fracture of both the bones of right lower limb.
Though he asserts that he was earning Rs.10,000/- p.m., but to substantiate the same, no documents are forthcoming.
The Tribunal has taken his monthly notional income at Rs.6,000/- p.m.
But, this Court is consistently taking income pertaining to accidents - 10 - NC: 2023:KHC:41430 of 2013 at Rs.8,000/- p.m.

In the absence of any material evidence, the income of the claimant is required to be taken as Rs.8,000/- p.m.
14.
The medical evidence discloses that the Doctor has deposed that the disability is 15.5% to the whole body.
The Tribunal has taken the disability at 10% but, the Doctor has not stated about the disability to a particular limb.
15. Considering these aspects, in my considered opinion disability can be taken at 8% to the whole body.
If the disability is taken at 8%, then the loss of future earning capacity would work out as Rs.8,000/- x 12 x 17 x 8/100 = Rs.1,30,560/-.
16. The Tribunal has awarded Rs.40,000/- under the head of pain and suffering which is based on a proper appreciation and does not call for any interference.
Accordingly, under the head of medical expenses Rs.70,280/- was awarded on the basis of records by the Tribunal, which is also just and proper.
Under the head of - 11 - NC: 2023:KHC:41430 loss of income during the laid up period Rs.30,000/- is awarded by the Tribunal, which is also based on proper appreciation.
Under the head of loss of happiness and amenities Rs.12,000/- is awarded by the Tribunal, which appears to be on lower side and I propose to award Rs.20,000/- under this head.
Towards future medical expenses was awarded by the Tribunal to the extent of Rs.10,000/, which does not call for any interference.

Hence, the claimant would be entitled for compensation under various heads as under:
1. Pain an sufferings Rs.40,000/-

2 . Medical expenses Rs.70,280/-
3. Loss of earning during the laid up Rs.30,000/-
period 4. Loss of future earning capacity Rs.1,30,560/-
5. Loss of happiness and amenities Rs.20,000/-

6 5.

Future medical expenses Rs.10,000/-
Total Rs.3,00,840/-
Hence, claimant would be entitled for total compensation of Rs.3,00,840/- as against Rs.2,84,680/-
awarded by the Tribunal.

In MFA No.4716/2015 arising out of MVC No.444/2013, appellants No.2 to 5, who are the claimants are not the dependents and they are not entitled for any compensation and entire compensation is required to be paid to claimant No.1/appellant No.1

Hence, both the appeals need to be allowed-in-part and accordingly, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER
(i) Both the appeals are allowed-in-part.

(ii) The claimant No.1 in MFA No.4716/2013 arising out of MVC No.444/2013 is held entitled for total compensation of Rs.9,43,600/- as against Rs.5,76,500/-
awarded by the Tribunal.
(iii) The appellant-claimant No.1 is the mother of the deceased and is alone entitled for entire compensation.
Out of compensation awarded 50% shall be released in her favour and balance shall be deposited in her name for a period of 3 years in any Nationalized Bank in F.D. scheme.
(iv) In MFA No.4717/2015 arising out of MVC No.445/2013, the claimant is held entitled for total compensation of Rs.3,00,840/- as against Rs.2,84,680/- awarded by the Tribunal.
(v) The enhanced compensation in both the cases shall carry interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of the petition.
(vi) The entire enhanced compensation in MFA No.4717/2015 shall be released in favour of claimant/appellant.
(vii) The entire compensation is required to be paid by respondent No.3 - Insurance Company.

rpc_texts: Under the head of - 11 - NC: 2023:KHC:41430 loss of income during the laid up period Rs.30,000/- is awarded by the Tribunal, which is also based on proper appreciation.
Under the head of loss of happiness and amenities Rs.12,000/- is awarded by the Tribunal, which appears to be on lower side and I propose to award Rs.20,000/- under this head.
Towards future medical expenses was awarded by the Tribunal to the extent of Rs.10,000/, which does not call for any interference.

Hence, the claimant would be entitled for compensation under various heads as under:
1. Pain an sufferings Rs.40,000/-

Future medical expenses Rs.10,000/-
Total Rs.3,00,840/-
Hence, claimant would be entitled for total compensation of Rs.3,00,840/- as against Rs.2,84,680/-
awarded by the Tribunal.

Hence, both the appeals need to be allowed-in-part and accordingly, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER

(ii) The claimant No.1 in MFA No.4716/2013 arising out of MVC No.444/2013 is held entitled for total compensation of Rs.9,43,600/- as against Rs.5,76,500/-
awarded by the Tribunal.
(iii) The appellant-claimant No.1 is the mother of the deceased and is alone entitled for entire compensation.
Out of compensation awarded 50% shall be released in her favour and balance shall be deposited in her name for a period of 3 years in any Nationalized Bank in F.D. scheme.
(iv) In MFA No.4717/2015 arising out of MVC No.445/2013, the claimant is held entitled for total compensation of Rs.3,00,840/- as against Rs.2,84,680/- awarded by the Tribunal.
(v) The enhanced compensation in both the cases shall carry interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of the petition.
(vi) The entire enhanced compensation in MFA No.4717/2015 shall be released in favour of claimant/appellant.
(vii) The entire compensation is required to be paid by respondent No.3 - Insurance Company.
